## SPECIAL INSTRUCTION-05 (REV-01)
## PROCEDURE FOR REPORTING THEFT OF DMRC PROPERTY, REGISTRATION OF FIR, RELEASE OF RECOVERED PROPERTY AND INSURANCE CLAIM
## 1. INTRODUCTION

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This procedure details guidelines for Reporting Theft of DMRC Property, Registration of FIR,  Release of Recovered Property and Insurance Claim.

## 1. INTRODUCTION

Rule 8 of The  Metro Railway General Rules, 2020 & Metro Railways General (Amendment) Rules, 2022 states:
## Prevention of trespass, damage or loss-

## Prevention of trespass, damage or loss-

Every Metro railway employee shall be responsible for the security and protection of the property of the Metro railway administration under his charge or possession.
Every Metro railway employee shall endeavour to prevent-
trespass on Metro railway premises;
theft, damage or loss of Metro railway property.
injury to passenger, others and himself; and
Fire and other unsafe incidents in Metro railway premises.
## 2. SCOPE

## 2. SCOPE

This procedure applies to Staff of Operation and Maintenance, who are the custodians of the  DMRC property.
## 3. OBJECTIVE

## 3. OBJECTIVE

3.1 Prompt registration of FIR at the concerned Police Station.
3.2 Aid to investigating agency.
3.3 Compilation of documents for
Police - For investigation
Finance/O&M - For insurance claim.
## 4. RESPONSIBILITIES
## 4.1 Custodian of the Assets of DMRC (Supervisor or above)

## 4.1 Custodian of the Assets of DMRC (Supervisor or above)

Inform  the  Metro  Police  Control  Room  at  Intercom  no.  514712,  landline  at  01122183903/04, Mobile no. at 8745001709, Fax at 011-22183905 or DMRP helpline no.  1511/112 for  Delhi  Metro  Rail  Police  jurisdiction,  and  112  for  local  police  and other state police jurisdictions.
Inform  the  CISF  control  room  at  011-22185556,  22183606,  intercom-600418, 600425, 600435, 600458, 600459, and mobile no. 9971959001 (for lines 1, 2, 7, 8, and  AEL)  and  011-23415065,  23413958,  intercom  502100,  502101,  502103,  and mobile no. 9821289002 (for lines 3, 4, 5, 6, and 9) or helpline no. at 155655/22185555 (SM-14 shall be referred).
Inform  concerned  Security  Inspector  and  WCSA  helpline  at  011-23415480  or 8800550490.

## Introduction

In case the response from concerned DMRP/Local Police Station/Tel. No. 112 is not satisfactory,  Custodian  of  asset  shall  inform  the  senior  officers  of  the Concerned Police  Station  {for  jurisdiction  wise  contact  details  of  SHO  (Station  House  Officer) and DO (Duty Officer), SM-14 shall be referred}.

## Introduction

Submit  the  written  complaint  to  the  SHO/SO/DO  of  the  concerned  Police  Station promptly or lodge e-FIR.
Compile all documents like copies of the logs maintained at OCC/ Station/ Depot/ O/o Custodian etc., photographs of the scene of occurrence, relevant extracts from stock  register,  site  plan  (sketch)  of  the  place  of  occurrence  etc.  required  by  the Investigating officer.
Preserve the scene of crime with the assistance of station controller, if feasible. No foreign object at scene of crime should be touched by hand.
In case of red handed capture by the Security/ other staff, hand over the recovered property to Police against proper receipt.
Provide assistance to police officials for facilitating the investigation.
Custodian of asset shall request to retain the video recording of the incident, as per procedure in vogue, for use in further investigation.
Inspect and survey the area along with Security Inspector, DMRP, JE/ASE/SE/SSE/Civil  or other concerned department and suggest corrective measures to prevent reoccurrence.
## 4.2 Station Controller

## 4.2 Station Controller

On getting information about theft from custodian of asset, Station Controller shall:
(a) Obtain all relevant information from custodian of asset such as name, contact no. of custodian, date & time of incident, details of asset theft etc. for record.
(b) Inform the CHC/OCC and Security Cell (Contact No011-23415480, 8800550490, 502232) about the incident along with all relevant details and shall make entry in station diary in this regard.
In  case  of  red  handed  capture  of  the  culprit  by  security/other  staff,  ensure  safe custody of the accused and hand over to the concerned Police authority.
Render  all  possible  assistance  to  Custodian  of  asset  and  Security  Inspector  for investigation.
Survey the area around scene of occurrence along with Custodian of asset, Security Inspector and Supervisor/civil and suggest corrective measures to prevent reoccurrence.
## 4.3 Chief Controller OCC

## 4.3 Chief Controller OCC

Inform all Senior Officers of concerned department.
Monitor  the  progress  of  events  at  place  of  incident  &  keep  the  Senior  Officers informed.
## 4.4 Security Cell

## 4.4 Security Cell

On getting information about theft from custodian of asset/ Station Controller on duty Security Inspector in WCSA helpline or WCSA helpline staff shall -,

## Introduction

Inform  Security  Inspector  (As  per  area  of  jurisdiction),  Senior  Officers  of  Security Wing & Chief Security Commissioner.

## Introduction

On getting  information,  Security  Inspector  (As  per  area  of  jurisdiction)  shall  reach the site of incident.
Security  Inspector  shall  accompany  the  concerned  staff  for  lodging  the  written complain/FIR  with  the  SHO/SO/DO  and  render  all  possible  assistance  to  the concerned staff.
Monitor  the  progress  of  events  at  place  of  incident  &  keep  the  Senior  Officers informed / updated. A detailed report of the case shall be prepared by the Security Inspector for onward submission to the Assistant Security Commissioner (ASC).
Security Inspector shall also remain present and assist to the concerned staff during any enquiry or investigation arising from or related to the said Complaint/FIR/e-FIR.
## 4.5 Assistant Security Commissioner

## 4.5 Assistant Security Commissioner

Submit a report regarding theft of DMRC property to CSC in consultation with Security Inspectors and suggest corrective measures to prevent reoccurrence.
## 4.6 Security Inspector

## 4.6 Security Inspector

Security Inspector shall appraise the details of incident to Assistant Security Commissioner. Security Inspector shall visit the site of incident in their respective lines and render all possible assistance to the concerned staff in lodging FIR. He should also survey  the  area  and  suggest  preventive  measures  to  prevent  reoccurrence  of  such cases.  Security  Inspector  shall  further  liaison  with  Concerned  Police  Station  (SM-14 shall be referred) and update concerned officials about progress of investigation.
## 5. INSTRUCTIONS FOR LODGING FIR

## 5. INSTRUCTIONS FOR LODGING FIR

First Information Report is not an encyclopedia and every minute detail is not required to be given  in  FIR,  but  a  First  Information  Report  should  contain  as  much  information  as  is available at the time of recording it. Therefore, the informant should incorporate the facts regarding name of witnesses, the entry/exit points of the offender and the traces left by the accused e.g. shoes, chappals, tools, bags, etc. at the spot while reporting the matter to the police.
5.1 FIR shall be lodged by the Metro employee who is in Custodian of the Assets of DMRC (supervisor or above) by filing a written complaint or lodge e-FIR at https://propertytheft.delhipolice.gov.in/Home.aspx for Delhi or Police website of concerned State Police.
5.2 Complaint should be handed over to the Police either at the spot or to the Duty Officer at  the  Police  Station  concerned  (for  jurisdiction  wise  contact  details  of  SHO  (Station House Officer) and DO (Duty Officer), SM-14 shall be referred) and one copy be sent to CSC office at fourth floor, Metro Bhawan, for information and necessary action either by DAK or through FAX (011- 23415836)
5.3 All relevant documents like photographs, site plan, logs etc. should be handed over to the Police as early as possible against proper receipt.
5.4 Words viz. missing/ lost shall not be used; instead, of stolen/ theft should be mentioned in the complaint to the Police.
5.5 Always  stick  to  the  facts  and  never  change  the  statement  under  pressure  so  as  to

## Introduction

avoid registration of a criminal case.

## Introduction

5.6 Request the Police for copy of the FIR for official record. In case of non-acceptance of complaint/ non-registration of FIR, concerned Security Inspector may be contacted. A report may be sent to O/o CSC for further necessary action.
## 6. INSURANCE CLAIM:

## 6. INSURANCE CLAIM:

As all the assets of DMRC are insured against fire, theft and burglary, an FIR which is a mandatory requirement for filing claim with the insurance company must be lodged with the Police.
All  custodians  of  the  DMRC  assets  are  duty  bound  to  comply  with  the  following instructions to file the insurance claim:
6.1 FIR must be lodged by the concerned wing for theft of Metro property without any delay.
6.2 Copy of FIR along with the incident report in the prescribed Performa Specimen Report at Annexure-'A' be sent to Finance/O&M for obtaining claim from Insurance company within 14 days of the incident.
6.3 Approximate cost of property/damage must be mentioned to work out the details of the claim.
6.4 Untraced report may be procured from the Police within three months for onwards transmission to insurance company through Manager/Finance/O&M.
## 7. Release of recovered articles on Supardari:

## 7. Release of recovered articles on Supardari:

The complainant of the case will file an application on ten rupees non-judicial stamp paper (Format at Annexure- C) in the concerned court (Annexure- B) for release of recovered articles.  After  obtaining court's  order for  release  of  property,  it  is to  be submitted  in the concerned police station for release of stolen/recovered property.

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

## 1.0  INTRODUCTION

This procedure delineates the guidelines regarding management of Roving Attendant (RA) for UTO mode of train operation (without RA) in line-07 & 08. This procedure is applicable only for RS-10 Trains. This instruction shall be read in conjunction with Metro Railway General Rules2020 & its amendment and relevant SOPs.
## 2.0  GENERAL

## 2.0  GENERAL

2.1 This instruction deals with the deployment and management of RA at strategic locations across Line-07 (MKPR-MUPR-SVVR) & Line 7 Ext. (MKPR- SNVH-MUPR) and Line-08 (BCGN-JPW) for smooth implementation of UTO mode of train operation (without RA) in staged manner.
2.2 For train operation in UTO mode, there must be provisions for Roving Attendant to intervene in case of failures or emergencies. As per MRGR 2020 'Roving Attendant' means an authorized person responsible for performing required functions in driverless or unattended train operation'.
3.0  Strategy for RA Deployment
## 3.1  For Line-7 (MKPR-MUPR- SVVR):

## 3.1  For Line-7 (MKPR-MUPR- SVVR):

At Line-07 (MKPR-MUPR- SVVR), UTO mode Stage-1 and Stage-2 are already implemented. At present, UTO mode Stage-2 is operational on Line 7(MKPR-MUPR-SVVR) and the RA may remain anywhere inside the train.
After successful completion of Stage 2, further transition to Stage 3 shall be done in progressive manner with approval of competent authority as detailed in following para:
Stage 3 A: This stage will be implemented, When UST pass percentage is ≥ 97% and RA/ETO intervention in the mid-section is ≤ 1 case per month. In this stage, RA shall be deployed in the alternate train who shall remain anywhere in the train. RA may be used/shifted in other trains as per the requirement.
ii)  Stage 3 B: This stage will be implemented, when UST pass percentage is ≥ 99% and RA/ETO intervention in the mid-section is ≤ 1 case per quarter. In this stage, RA may be withdrawn from trains and shall be placed at strategic stations only (during 0700 hours to 2130 hours) as detailed vide table-01. This arrangement shall be reviewed time to time & accordingly, RA deployed at station may be increased, decreased, or withdrawn as required.

## 4.0  Procedure

## 4.0  Procedure

4.1 Concerned crew control shall be responsible for deployment of RA's.
4.2 RA shall report to crew control or as per the location given in Table and Sign On as per procedure in  vogue.  RA  shall  then  report  to  deployed  location.  The  RA  shall  always  be  available  at designated location throughout his duty shift and same shall be monitored by concerned crew control.
4.3 In case of occurrence of such failures/ scenario which cannot be rectified at OCC level and/or need  arises  to  be  attended  by  RA,  TC/OCC  in  co-ordination  with  ACC/OCC  shall  inform concerned Crew Control to instruct RA to board the train(s).
4.4 In case, RA is required to go other than designated location for taking the charge of train, Suitable arrangement shall be made for the movement of RA to the desired location.
4.5 RA shall board/de-board the train as per procedure detailed vide Safety circular-27C.
4.6 After completion of assistance/intervention duty, RA shall go back to his designated location after getting confirmation from TC/OCC and inform the same to concerned Crew control.
4.7 ACC/OCC shall maintain the record of boarding/de- boarding of RA & UTO suspension, if any.

## 4. GENERAL

## PROCEDURE TO ENSURE NO TRAIN ENTERS THE DEPOT OR STABLED AT OUTSTATIONS WITH ANY UNAUTHORISED PERSON ON LINE -7 & 8
## 1. INTRODUCTION

## 1. INTRODUCTION

This Special Instruction delineates the responsibility of the Station Controller & Traffic Controller to  ensure  no  train  enters  the  depot  or  stabled  at  outstations  (at  platform  or  siding)  with  any unauthorised person on Line - 7 & 8.
## 2. SCOPE

## 2. SCOPE

This  procedure  is  applicable  for  Line-7  &  8  and  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  the  Metro Railways General Rules, 2020 its Amendments, Safety Circulars and other instructions in vogue. However, this Special instruction shall supersede para 16.3.7 of SOP Station (Rev-01).
## 3. GENERAL
## 3. GENERAL

OCC shall design time table in a manner so that trains planned for depot or for the outstation stabling shall not move further from terminal/ intermediate terminal station until verified that no unauthorised person is inside the train. TC/OCC shall apply Train Hold (in case Train is in NonUTO Mode of operation, TC shall instruct RA/ETO to hold the train and take confirmation from SC that the train is empty before sending it to depot or for the outstation stabling.
To ensure that no train enters the depot or stabled at outstations (at platform or siding) with any unauthorised person-
(i) Traffic Controller shall inform the concerned Station Controller regarding train termination well before reaching the train at terminal/intermediate terminal station from where the empty train shall depart for the depot or for the outstation stabling.
(ii) Station Controller of terminal/intermediate terminal station shall remain available at platform before reaching the train at station and shall confirm his availability to Traffic Controller in group mode.
(iii) On reaching the train at terminal/ intermediate terminal station from where the empty train shall depart either for the depot or for the outstation stabling, Information Controller shall make  announcements  inside  the  train  for  information  of  passengers  regarding  train termination and guide to vacate the train.
(iv) Station Controller shall physically verify that train is empty and no passenger is left inside the train. Station Controller shall communicate the same to TC/OCC in group mode.
(v) TC on receiving the message from Station Controller shall give door close command and reconfirm that no passenger has boarded the train during closing of train doors. In case, Train is in Non-UTO Mode of operation, TC shall instruct on-board RA/ETO to close the doors.

(v) TC on receiving the message from Station Controller shall give door close command and reconfirm that no passenger has boarded the train during closing of train doors. In case, Train is in Non-UTO Mode of operation, TC shall instruct on-board RA/ETO to close the doors.
(vi) After confirmation from Station Controller, TC shall give the departure command for further movement of train  to  Depot/outstation  stabling.  In  case,  Train  is  in  Non-UTO  Mode  of operation, further movement for stabling shall be done as per procedure in vogue.

Failure of Information Controller Radio control workstation (IC RCW).
There are 2 IC RCW available for each Line- 7 & 8 in OCC Metro Bhawan. In UTO mode, Passenger Emergency Call (PEC) from train is transferred to both IC RCWs any of the IC can answer the call.
Live and Pre-recorded announcements are also made by the IC in trains by IC RCW Panel.
In  case  of  failure  of  one  IC  RCW,  another  IC  RCW  is  available  for  answering  the Passenger Emergency Call/Live PA/Pre-recorded PA. There will be no effect on the Train Operation.
If both the IC RCW of L-7 & 8 OCC Metro Bhawan fails than control is transferred to the RCW of BOCC (Back up OCC at Vinod Nagar).
In  case  of  failure  of  one  or  both  OCC  IC  RCW  and  BCC  IC  RCW,  same  shall  be informed to Telecom Controller by respective IC.
If  all  RCW  of  OCC  and  BOCC  fail  then  PAD  calls  could  not  be  forwarded  to OCC/BOCC. In that case, failure shall be informed to Telecom Controller by TC/OCC and TC/OCC should also instruct to all the TO/RA/ETO to take charge of the train and  operate  the  train  in  Non-UTO  mode.  In  non-UTO  mode  PEC  calls  shall  be forward to RA/TO/ETO on MOU (main operating unit in cab).

Failure of On- Board CCTV.

## 3. Signal Visibility: -

Signal  visibility  for  line  1  to  line  6:Signals  on  Main  Lines  and  Depot  Arrival  and Departure  Tracks  shall  afford  adequate  Sighting  Distance  that  will  enable  a  Train Operator  to  brake  a  Train  from  25  Kmph  Speed  to  Stop  before  reaching  the  Fixed Signal therefore the sighting distance at 25 kmph shall not be less than 100 meter.

Signal  visibility  for  AEL:  Signals  on  Main  Lines  and  Depot  Arrival  and  Departure Tracks  shall  afford  adequate  Sighting  Distance  that  will  enable  a  Train  Operator  to brake a Train from 25 Kmph Speed to Stop before reaching the Fixed Signal therefore the sighting distance at 25 kmph shall not be less than 100 meter.

## 5. Role and Responsibility of Signal Sighting Committee:

The  Committee  shall  inspect  available  signal  aspect  of  available  signals  (along  with route  indicators)  during  revenue  hours  and  remaining  signal  aspects  and  all  other signals (along with route indicators) including signals for reverse movement of direction during  non  -revenue  hours  on  main  line. ## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  procedure  delineates  the  guidelines  regarding  management  of  Emergency  Train  Operator (ETO) for UTO mode of train operation (without RA) in line-07 & 08.

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION

This  instruction  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railway  General  Rules-2020  &  its amendment and relevant SOPs.
## 2.0 GENERAL
## 2.0 GENERAL

2.1 'Unattended Train Operation (UTO)' means a train operation with no regulatory requirement of Roving Attendant on-board the train and emergency handling or abnormal situation shall be handled by system or through special instruction;
However, in case of failures or emergencies in UTO mode (without RA) of train operation, the intervention of ETO/RA may be essential in one or more train as per the scenario.
As per MRGR 2020 and its amendments:
'Emergency Train Operator (ETO) means an authorised person having valid certificate of competency for train operation, nominated by Traffic Controller to drive the train in an emergency '
"Roving  Attendant"  means  an  authorised  person  responsible  for  performing  required functions in driverless or unattended train operation. This function shall be managed by authorised person from active train operation.
2.2 As per extant DMRC policy, Executives and Supervisors of technical department other than those staff in active Train Operations are also required to undergo train driving training and possess  valid  competency  for  the  train  driving  in  respective  line.  Hence,  all  technical departments shall ensure that staff/executive posted on UTO enabled lines (Line-7 & 8) shall possess valid train driving competency for the concerned line as per extant DMRC policy.
2.3 It shall be the duty of the concerned Executive/ Supervisor (as mentioned in para 2.2 above) to keep themselves updated with the extant train operations procedures for train driving/ Line specific  instructions  from  DMRC  intranet  link https://intranet.dmrc.org/tsnew/index.php and to perform at least one round trip train handling in presence of competent Train Operator once in a month, to ensure that competency certification remains active.

2.4 Staff/Executive trained and possessing valid competency as per para 2.2 & 2.3 above can be utilized as ETO by the TC/OCC whenever the situation arises to do so. Staff in active train operations in concerned line shall be utilized as RA to be managed by the concerned crew control.
2.5 A Kit bag comprising of MASCON Key, PSL Key, Square Key and Tetra Hand Set shall be maintained  at  SCR  for  use  of  ETO.  Concerned  Station  Manager  shall  be  responsible  for upkeep of Kit bag and charging of Tetra Sets.

## 1.0  Instruction  for  reversal  of  train  in  emergency  situation  which  has  not  completed  the authorized movement on Line- 7 & 8

## 1.0  Instruction  for  reversal  of  train  in  emergency  situation  which  has  not  completed  the authorized movement on Line- 7 & 8

The following steps shall be followed for reversal of train which has not completed the authorized movement in emergency situation: -
## i. For Line-7: -

## i. For Line-7: -

TC/OCC shall bring the train to a halt by giving stop train command to the train.
TC/OCC shall release the set route through 'Emergency Route Release' command.
TC/OCC shall set the route of the train in reverse DOT up to the nearest station.
IC shall make necessary announcements in the train to make the passengers aware that train will move in reverse direction due to emergency situation ahead.
TC/OCC shall give start train command to the train to move in reverse DOT.
## ii. For Line-8: -

## ii. For Line-8: -

TC/OCC shall bring the train to a halt by giving remote EB command to the train.
TC/OCC shall enable the Emergency mode on ATS MMI.
TC/OCC shall set the route of the train in reverse DOT upto the nearest station by firing the route through virtual emergency mode signals.
IC shall make necessary announcements in the train to make the passengers aware that train will move in reverse direction due to emergency situation ahead.
TC/OCC shall release the remote EB command from the train.
TC/OCC shall give departure command to the train to move in reverse DOT.
## iii. Precautions to be Taken for Crowd Management:

## iii. Precautions to be Taken for Crowd Management:

TC/OCC shall inform other Controllers in the OCC regarding reversal of train and to initiate required action. TC/OCC shall also inform Station Controller of adjacent stations about the reversal pattern due to emergency and change (if any) of platform for boarding and/or  de boarding.  SC  shall  ensure  suitable  announcement  in  the  station  and  guide  passengers accordingly.
On  the  basis  of  information  received  from  Traffic  Controller,  IC  shall  make  suitable announcements inside the train(s).
TC/OCC shall ensure that no other train shall enter in the section where emergency reversal of train is processed, by suitable commands.
Before  starting  any  movement  in  reversal  TC  should  ensure  that  there  is  no  train  in section/platform before giving start command for reverse DOT.

## ii. For Line-: -08

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION:

## 1.0 INTRODUCTION:

The Visual Alarm System is an emergency safety mechanism designed to alert Train Operators of potential hazards or incidents. In the event of an emergency, the look-out person deployed at platform can activate a flashing light (Visual Alarm System) located at a position visible from the train operator's cab. This Alarm System serves as an immediate alert, prompting the train operator to take swift action in stopping the train.
## 2.0 SCOPE:

## 2.0 SCOPE:

This procedure order delineates the roles and responsibilities of TC/OCC, Train Operator and Station  Controller  in  case  of  any  untoward  situation  at  the  time  of  closing  of  train  doors/ departure of train.
This  JPO  shall  be  read  in  conjunction  with  Metro  Railways  General  Rules-2020  &  its amendments and other relevant rules and procedures in vogue.
## 3.0 VISUAL ALARM SYSTEM

## 3.0 VISUAL ALARM SYSTEM

3.1 Visual Alarm Systems are installed beyond platform at some stations of the Line-1, 3 & 4, attached as Annexure -A . Annexure A details the location of stations/Platform, where the Visual Alarm System is installed and also describes CFA deployment.
3.2 Visual Alarm System consists of an LED light and a Remote by which when operated causes LED light to flash in blue and red colours. The pictures of the Visual Alarm System and its remote device are attached as Annexure B.
3.3 The LED light of Visual Alarm remains 'OFF' under normal conditions. It continues flashing when activated from the remote by the lookout person, in unusual scenarios.
To reset the LED light, it should be 'Turned OFF' manually.
## 4.0 GENERAL:

## 4.0 GENERAL:

## 1. INTRODUCTION:

For  indicating  the  powered/un-powered  status  of  an  OHE  section  (Feeding  post  to  Neutral section/Dead End), two PTs (One PT of the first elementary section towards the feeding post and another PT of the last elementary section towards the neutral section/Dead end) are used with the 'OR Logic'. i.e., In case either one or both PTs indicate powered, the OHE section shall be considered as Powered however, in case both PTs indicate unpowered, OHE section shall be considered as Unpowered.

## 3. DEBOARDING  OF  PASSENGERS  WITHOUT  RA/ETO  INTERVENTION  IN  CASE  OF EMERGENCY :-

Whenever any train  is  stalled  in  mid-section  and  due  to  any  unforeseen  circumstances  / failures,  immediate  de-boarding  of  passenger  is  required  and  waiting  for  RA/ETO  is  not advisable  then  TC/OCC  shall  plan  for  immediate  de-boarding  or  self-evacuation  without RA/ETO intervention.
3.1 In the case of extreme emergency, when the safety of passengers is at risk, Chief Controller in  consultation  with  HOD/Ops  or  Dy.  HOD/Ops  shall  plan  for  the  detrainment  of  the passengers.

3.9 TC/IC/other  controllers  shall  continually  observe  the  camera  view  of  emergency  door through LVS during de-boarding process and act accordingly.

## 3.0 GENERAL:

TC shall ensure that there is no Train moving in the section in reverse direction.

TC shall  set  route  manually  in  desired  direction  up-to  next  interlocking  station  of  affected station  using  relevant  crossover  and  execute  departure  command  guide  IC  for  relevant announcements inside concerned train.

## 3.0 GENERAL GUIDELINES

3.1 In  case  a  Train  Operator  notices  a  person  on  the  running  or  in  the  proximity  of  track  /  in gesture to access the tracks, TO shall immediately apply Emergency break (EB) to stop the train and report the matter to TC/OCC.
3.2 In case Train stops short of the person,
TO shall report the same to the TC/OCC.
The TC/OCC shall stop the train movement on both the tracks.
TC/OCC shall instruct SC to reach the site.
SC  shall  rush  to  the  incident  site  and  clear  the  track  section  with  the  help  of  station/ security staff.
If  any  medical assistance is required SC shall provide  first-aid to the injured person and further, if required the injured person shall be sent to hospital immediately.
3.3 If passenger got hit and/or run-over by the train

TC/OCC shall stop train movement on both the lines and instruct the on duty SC to reach the incident site.
